expectations.text: Rejects the operational/degraded/major severity taxonomy for the event's status page.
expectations.evidence: "Operational / degraded / major outage levels | ❌ Replace"

expectations.text: States why the taxonomy fails: an event's disruptions are discrete and human-scale, and classifying adds a step during the minutes with least to spare - message classes replace the tiers.
expectations.evidence: "Event disruptions are discrete and human-scale. Tiers also add a classification step in the minutes you have least of."

expectations.text: Rejects the subscribe-for-updates form as assuming a long service relationship nobody has with a two-day conference.
expectations.evidence: "Nobody subscribes to a two-day conference's status feed."

expectations.text: Rejects the public post-mortem and routes the written incident note to the internal debrief instead, because a public cause writeup is a liability when the cause is frequently a person or a supplier.
expectations.evidence: "Make it internal... cause is often a person or a supplier"; "full review as a note for event-debrief."

expectations.text: Keeps the status page itself, because the livestream and the shuttle are things an attendee cannot see the state of for themselves.
expectations.evidence: "✅ Keep... the livestream, the shuttle and the entrance."

expectations.text: States the status page is never a push channel: nobody checks it unprompted, and it only works with a push on another channel pointing at it.
expectations.evidence: "The page is a destination that a push points at."

expectations.text: Rejects posting daily logistics (lunch, badge desk hours) on the status page because non-incident content trains people to ignore the page.
expectations.evidence: "trains people to ignore the page."

expectations.text: Routes day logistics to an hours-scale surface such as the chat broadcast channel or on-site screens instead.
expectations.evidence: "Their first channel is the chat broadcast channel, with on-site screens as a second."

expectations.text: Rejects hosting the page on the registration server: the page must survive the outage it reports and stay editable from a phone in under a minute.
expectations.evidence: "editable from a phone in under a minute"; "fails with it."

expectations.text: Keeps timestamped updates on a fixed interval, including explicit no-change updates, because silence during an outage reads as abandonment.
expectations.evidence: Tier 2: "even if nothing changed ('still working on it, next update by 11:30')".

expectations.text: Keeps a written resolution stating when the incident ended and what actually happened.
expectations.evidence: Resolution template: "Resolved at [time]. [What happened...]"

expectations.text: Establishes the page as the single canonical surface that every other channel points at rather than restates.
expectations.evidence: Says to point at the page from the list, but never states other channels point rather than restate.

expectations.text: Fixes the update interval before the event and writes it into the routing rule, because an interval chosen during an outage is chosen badly.
expectations.evidence: "Proposed starting intervals, to be fixed before the event".
